newsitem.title: CHINA: China soybean buying seen unlikely on price jump.
newsitem.headline: China soybean buying seen unlikely on price jump.

text.p: China was unlikely to buy soybeans at current prices, although they may well have been making enquiries in the market, traders said on Tuesday. "This is really too high for Chinese buyers," said one dealer, noting that markets were very quiet. Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) November soybeans ended up 18 cents at $6.19-1/4 per bushel, aided by talk that China was looking to buy 200,000 tonnes of new crop U.S. soybeans.

"Maybe they were interested, it's too bad the prices jumped up before any deals," said one trader. Soybean meal had jumped too, with September delivery soymeal heard quoted in the low US$280's per tonne, C&F China. "If the prices do not improve, we are really looking at a period where nothing is going to happen," said one dealer, noting his desk was devoid of enquiries.
China's buying interest for meal still rested between $265 and $270 per tonne, C&F China.
